summary: Unexpected GPU scarcity during high fanout; prefetch locks and allocator throttling
description:
Issue summary:
Customer VertexHealth experienced sudden throughput collapse on their dedicated pool during midday traffic spike with many short chat fanouts. Traffic profile: high fanout of short streams (avg tokens/stream ~40) with a metadata-heavy prefetch pattern.

Impact:
- Customer observed p99 token latency spike from ~120ms to ~2.4s across routed model variants.
- Requests began receiving allocator attach delays (attach_time spikes) and a subset of short streams failed with 504s on the client side.
- Customer reported visible increased costs due to retries and fallback to hosted tier.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id d-pool-vertex-03 (prod-us-west)
- Models: redwood/gpt-13b-v2-quant pinned for customer routes; fallback to 7b quant during capacity fallbacks
- Infra: nvidia-A100 heterogeneous mix; allocator version: v2.8.1; prefetcher: v1.4.0

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Run high fanout load: 60k short streams over 10 minutes with average concurrency ~120 per tenant shard.
2) Enable prefix prefetch with aggressive TTL refresh (~30s) and small kv-cache budget per stream.
3) Observe attach_time and p99 token latency across the pool.

Observed logs / snippets:
- allocator: "attach_delay=1123ms attach_retry=3 slot_wait=87ms reason=allocator-throttle"
- prefetcher: "prefetch_lock_acquired stream_id=xxxx duration=1450ms kv_growth=+40MB"
- runtime kernel: "nvlink_io_wait=high pci_stall=intermittent kernel_queue_depth=low"

Notes: this is not the usual long-lived-ephemeral-snapshotter pattern; noise appears tied to many concurrent short sessions and aggressive prefetch TTLs that are causing transient kv-cache growth and prefetch locks which in turn starve allocator attach bandwidth for new attaches.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: aggressive per-stream prefetch TTLs + high fanout produce rapid kv-cache growth and frequent lock acquisition. Prefetcher holds locks while performing NVMe reads/writes to populate KV pagefiles; at peak concurrency this generates IO bursts causing node-level PCIe/NVMe backpressure. Backpressure delays runtime kernel io and allocator attach flows, causing attach_time spikes and effective GPU scarcity.

Telemetry checked:
- allocator attach histogram (pool d-pool-vertex-03): saw 90th->99th percentile jump coincident with prefetcher lock durations >800ms.
- node io wait: elevated during incident window (iostat, blktrace attached in confluence).
- kernel_queue_depth: low while io_wait high -> suggests compute waiting on IO.

Reproduced locally by: synthetic short-stream fanout + enabling prefetch TTL=30s; reproduced attach spikes and nvlink_io_wait.

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Reduced prefetch TTL to 120s across pool (soft config) — decreased lock churn but did not fully eliminate p99 spikes.
- Increased allocator concurrent attaches by +25% (hotfix) — improved attach tail once prefetch flush reduced.
resolution:
Short-term workaround (applied 2026-03-11):
- Rolled soft-config to VertexHealth pool: prefetch TTL increased to 120s and aggressive refresh disabled.
- Applied allocator hotfix to increase attach concurrency and to throttle prefetcher when node IO exceeds threshold.

Observed result: p99 improved from ~2.4s -> ~350ms; customer retries and timeouts reduced by ~92%.

Long-term action items (tracking):
- Infra: add NVMe IO reservation / QoS for dedicated pools to prevent tenant prefetch IO from impacting attach path (owner: Maya Rodriguez, ETA 2026-04-01).
- Runtime: implement non-blocking prefetch locks or lock-free KV staging to avoid long critical sections (owner: Alejandro Cruz, RFC due 2026-03-20).
- Allocator: enhance attach prioritization to favor short streams under high-fanout scenarios (owner: Ethan Bernstein, PR in review).
- Product: add documentation & console toggle for per-pool prefetch aggressiveness; recommended defaults for dedicated customers with high short-stream fanout.

Follow-up: schedule a post-incident review with VertexHealth and cross-team stakeholders; planned for 2026-03-18.
root_cause_summary: Transient node-level IO backpressure caused by aggressive per-stream prefetch behavior under high short-stream fanout. Prefetch locks and NVMe activity created IO stalls that delayed allocator attach and runtime IO, producing an apparent GPU scarcity (attach_time spikes) and throughput degradation.
resolution_status: Partial mitigation applied; monitoring continues. Permanent fixes are in roadmap and owners assigned.
